chapters.1.lds: The selected lesson studies the problem of turning toward another message. Why does Paul distinguish revelation from instruction by the earlier apostles?
chapters.1.summary: Paul writes to the assemblies of Galatia as an apostle sent by Jesus Christ. He gives no thanks. He is amazed that they are turning so quickly to a different good news. He says anyone who brings another message is cursed. His message did not come from a human source. He once persecuted the assembly and advanced in Judaism. God called him, and he went to Arabia, not to Jerusalem. After three years he visited Peter for fifteen days and saw James.
chapters.2.lds: How does Peter’s meal withdrawal conflict with the earlier shared recognition?
chapters.2.summary: After fourteen years Paul goes to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus. Titus, a Greek, is not forced to be circumcised. James, Peter, and John give Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship. They ask only that he remember the poor. In Antioch Peter eats with Gentiles, then draws back when men come from James. Barnabas is carried along too. Paul rebukes Peter before everyone. He says a person is justified by faith in Christ, not by law.
chapters.3.lds: The selected lesson connects receiving the Spirit with the gospel’s freedom. Why can the later law not cancel Abraham’s earlier promise?
chapters.3.summary: Paul calls the Galatians foolish and asks how they received the Spirit. It was by hearing with faith, not by works of the law. Abraham believed God, and those of faith are his children. The law curses all who fail to keep it, and Christ redeemed us. The promise to Abraham came 430 years before the law. The law cannot cancel it. The law was a tutor to bring us to Christ. In Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female.
chapters.4.lds: The selected lesson studies Paul’s appeal against returning to bondage. Why must the two mothers’ roles here remain part of Paul’s stated comparison?
chapters.4.summary: Paul says an heir who is a child is no different from a servant. God sent his Son, born of a woman, to redeem those under the law. Now they are sons and call God Abba, Father. He asks why they turn back to weak principles and observe days and seasons. He recalls how they welcomed him when he was ill. He is in labor again until Christ is formed in them. Then he tells of Abraham’s two sons, by Hagar and by the free woman. He says believers are children of the free woman.
chapters.5.lds: The selected lesson teaches freedom through love and conduct shaped by the Spirit. How does freedom become service rather than permission to harm others?
chapters.5.summary: Paul tells the Galatians to stand firm in freedom. If they accept circumcision, they must keep the whole law. What counts is faith working through love. He says a little yeast leavens the whole lump. They were called to freedom, to serve one another through love. The whole law is fulfilled in loving a neighbor as oneself. He lists the works of the flesh and then the fruit of the Spirit. The fruit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control.
chapters.6.lds: The selected lesson teaches patient work and the later consequences of choices. How do shared burdens and personal examination support each other?
chapters.6.summary: Paul tells the spiritual to restore gently anyone caught in a fault. They should bear one another’s burdens. Each should test his own work and carry his own load. A person reaps what he sows, to the flesh or to the Spirit. They should not grow tired of doing good, especially to the household of faith. Paul writes the ending in large letters with his own hand. He says those pressing circumcision want to avoid persecution. He will boast only in the cross, and a new creation is what counts.
